result: {"findings":[{"severity":"error","path":"spec.md","line":11,"quote":"- The form and its endpoint require a signed-in user, and contacts are created in that user's account.","claim":"The sign-in and account-ownership requirement has no acceptance criterion, so a build that lets anonymous users import, or creates contacts in the wrong account, would pass every listed check.","reproduce":"sed -n '/^## Acceptance/,$p' spec.md | grep -qiE 'signed-in|signed in|signed-out|signed out|unauthenticated|anonymous'"},{"severity":"warning","path":"spec.md","line":28,"quote":"- When a file has 10,001 rows or is over 5 MB, the system shall refuse it and create nothing.","claim":"The criterion lumps two limits into one line and names no boundary cases (exactly 10,000 rows accepted, exactly 5 MB accepted), nor does it check that the refusal shows the reason and limit; an off-by-one in either limit would go unnoticed.","reproduce":"sed -n '/^## Acceptance/,$p' spec.md | grep -q '10,000 rows'"},{"severity":"warning","path":"spec.md","line":15,"quote":"- Each import gets a batch id, and the summary offers 'Undo this import', which deletes that batch.","claim":"Undo is specified in the design but has no acceptance criterion, so there is no check that it deletes only that batch's contacts.","reproduce":"sed -n '/^## Acceptance/,$p' spec.md | grep -qi 'undo'"},{"severity":"warning","path":"spec.md","line":27,"quote":"- When a file has a wrong header, the system shall refuse it and create nothing.","claim":"The criterion does not check the required refusal message, and it names no edge cases such as an empty file or a header-only file, whose expected results are undefined.","reproduce":"sed -n '/^## Acceptance/,$p' spec.md | grep -qiE 'empty file|header-only|name,email,phone'"}]}
